name: ancient red dragon

special_abilities.name: legendary resistance
special_abilities.desc: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: The dragon can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

actions.name: bite
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) fire damage.

actions.name: claw
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d6 + 10) slashing damage.

actions.name: tail
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: frightful presence
actions.desc: Each creature of the dragon's choice that is within 120 feet of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: fire breath
actions.desc: The dragon exhales fire in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw, taking 91 (26d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

legendary_actions.name: detect
legendary_actions.desc: The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

legendary_actions.name: tail attack
legendary_actions.desc: The dragon makes a tail attack.

legendary_actions.name: wing attack (costs 2 actions)
legendary_actions.desc: The dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 15 ft. of the dragon must succeed on a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

lore:
The Ancient Red Dragon, or *Ignis Rex*, is the living personification of cataclysm. These titans claim the sulfurous maws of active volcanoes or the jagged, oxygen-starved heights of the world’s spine. They do not merely hunt; they subjugate. A Red’s predatory style is one of calculated devastation—descending like a falling star to bathe entire valleys in alchemical flame, consuming only what has been thoroughly seared. They are uniquely spiteful, known to track the descendants of those who once offended them, turning a hunt into a multi-generational vendetta.

In the tapestries of local folklore, they are "The Scourge of the Noon-Day." Commoners whisper that the sun itself hides behind clouds to avoid the dragon’s jealous gaze. They are the architects of ash, whose presence signals the death of kingdoms and the birth of a wasteland. To the mountain-dwellers, a tremor in the earth is not a tectonic shift, but the dragon’s arrogant laughter vibrating through the bedrock. To encounter one is to stand before a god of ruin, where gold is bedded in the charcoal of heroes.
